title: [clinic · EX-16] Price your own k
body:
> **Exercise clinic.** One long-running thread per exercise. Ask here rather than opening a
> new thread — the answers accumulate where the next person will look for them.
>
> **Exercise:** [`EX-16` — Price your own k](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/30-learning/exercises/ex-16-price-your-own-k.md) · difficulty 🟡

## What this exercise asks

Read the exercise first; this thread is for when you are stuck, not instead of it.

## Three ways people get stuck on this one

**1.** Pricing tokens and stopping. Notebook 07 and [#32](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/discussions/32) both make the point that generation tokens are roughly a third of a real bill.

**2.** Choosing `k` on `full_chain_recall` alone. It keeps climbing while `answer_correct` peaks and turns over around `k≈12–16`.

**3.** Ignoring `context_precision`, which is the column that shows the cost of a large `k` in quality rather than money.

## How to ask here

Post the **numbers you got**, the **config that produced them**, and **what you already tried**.
A question with a measurement in it gets answered in one round trip; a question without one
takes three.

If you have finished it, post the write-up in **Show and Tell** with the
`[solution · EX-16]` prefix rather than here — this thread stays for people who are stuck.
